text:
Ben Carter: For final readout (Week 3), we need to lock: (1) which cuts of data we’re showing, (2) who’s presenting which sections, (3) what’s “good enough” to call a winner vs iterate. Can we align today so I can start building the deck.

Tyler Benson: +1. Also want to make sure we don’t end up with 12 charts that all say the same thing :)

Soojin Lee: From a messaging POV, I’d love a clean narrative: baseline → what changed → what moved → what we’ll ship. Cuts should support the story, not overwhelm.

Camila Reyes: Agree. Keep it exec-friendly. If we have deep cuts, put them in appendix.

Ben Carter: Proposed structure:
- 5 min: goal + activation definition + experiment overview (me)
- 10 min: results (Sana)
- 5 min: learnings + next sprint recs (me)
- 5 min: risks/guardrails + roll-forward plan (Tyler + Marissa?)

Sana Farid: Works. For results section, I’d propose we show:
1) Activation rate within 24h + 72h (primary)
2) Time-to-first-success (median + p75)
3) D7 and D14 retention (directional; call out power limits)
4) Secondary milestones: billing_added, route_created, invite_teammate (mostly as leading indicators)

Mei Lin: Re: cuts — I think we *must* split new vs returning/lapsed. Retargeting impact is basically invisible otherwise.

Tyler Benson: Yes. We’ve got campaign touches joined to product events now, but it’s noisy if we combine cohorts.

Ben Carter: Ok. So main breakdowns:
- New signups (net-new accounts)
- “Returning” = previously signed up but no first_success in last 30 days?
- Lapsed users = had first_success historically but no usage in last 30 days?

Sana Farid: Careful: definitions. We should align with the taxonomy doc / what we actually built. I can do:
- New = first_seen_user_ts in window
- Non-activated signup = signed up in window, no first_request_success within 72h
- Lapsed = had first_request_success >30 days ago, no request_success in last 30 days
(assuming we’re doing this at user_id level, not org)

Mei Lin: +1 user-level. If we do org-level, we get weirdness with teammates.

Marissa Cole: For console nudges, I want a cut by “console exposure” too. At least: assigned experiment group vs holdout for checklist + banners.

Tyler Benson: We can do that. We have the bucketing property in the event payload (`experiment_assignment`). It’s clean for console. Email is more “received/opened/clicked” though.

Sana Farid: For email, I’d keep the readout to *intention-to-treat* (eligible/assigned to sequence vs suppressed/holdout), and then one slide on engagement (open/click) with deliverability guardrails.

Soojin Lee: +1. Also please avoid claiming “emails caused X” if it’s observational.

Ben Carter: On “by SDK” — do we want that in main deck or appendix?

Mei Lin: Appendix. The TS SDK changes might have improved time-to-first-success, but mixing it into the main narrative adds too many caveats.

Sana Farid: I can do one sanity chart: activation@72h by SDK family (TS/Python/Other) for new users only. But I’d keep it in appendix unless there’s a big divergence.

Tyler Benson: Another cut I’d recommend: region (NA/EU/APAC). We saw higher error rates in APAC week 1. Might matter for time-to-first-success.

Marissa Cole: If we include region, please add a note whether any console performance/SLO issues were observed. Sean asked me to ensure we call out guardrails.

Ben Carter: Guardrails slide will be explicit: unsubscribes, complaint rate, support tickets tagged “onboarding”, console perf.

Tyler Benson: For unsubscribes/complaints: I’ll pull daily rates + spike check. We did have that suppression bug early (SUP-2849). We should mention we fixed it and when.

Camila Reyes: Mention it, but keep it factual and brief: “issue discovered, mitigated, no ongoing risk.” Don’t turn the readout into a postmortem.

Ethan Wallace: For proof points/benchmarks referenced in retargeting, do we want one slide with “what we said” + substantiation links? Could help prevent questions.

Soojin Lee: Yes, but again appendix. In main deck I only want one line: “creative used benchmark messaging; no claim changes mid-flight.” Then appendix has the sources.

Ben Carter: Cool. Who presents what:
- Ben: intro + narrative + next steps
- Sana: results + stats caveats
- Tyler: attribution/UTM + email guardrails + retargeting performance
- Marissa: console nudge rollout + what shipped / what’s behind flag
Camila: you want to close / decision ask?

Camila Reyes: I can do 2 min close + decision framing. Keep it crisp: what we’re rolling forward, what we’re stopping, and what needs resourcing.

Sana Farid: One more question: do we want to define “activation” as first_request_success (2xx completion) or first_streaming_success?

Ben Carter: We decided primary = first_request_success (2xx) within 72h, right? Streaming is secondary milestone.

Marissa Cole: Yes. Product thread concluded that. Streaming is “higher-quality activation” but too restrictive as primary.

Tyler Benson: Works for me, also maps to email CTAs more cleanly.

Mei Lin: Please add a footnote that first_request_success requires `completion_reason != error` and status_code 2xx (or whatever is in the schema). We had the missing property issue in week 1.

Sana Farid: Yep. I’ll include a data quality note slide (appendix) with known instrumentation hiccups + how we filtered.

Ben Carter: Action items:
- Sana: draft results section + list of final cuts by EOD tomorrow
- Tyler: guardrails + attribution slides + retargeting perf summary
- Marissa: console rollouts / screenshots / flag status
- Soojin: review claims + tone + ensure we don’t overstate causality
I’ll assemble into the readout template and share for async comments.

Soojin Lee: Sounds good. Drop the deck in the #marketing channel when ready and tag me for claim review.

Camila Reyes: Please send me a 1-page summary version too (bullets). I’ll use it for exec staff.

Ben Carter: Will do. (reactions: :thumbsup: x4)
